   365	def check_fix_gates(repo_root: Path, branch: str, base: str, head_sha: str) -> str:
   366	    """Gate 6 — refuse while the serialized fix loop is mid-flight.
   367	    Returns the merge base (gate 7 scans the same commit range); the fix-prefixed
   368	    commit count is reported, never enforced (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-02)."""
   369	    # autofix.sh holds a mkdir-based lease keyed on the BRANCH (autofix.sh:580,
   370	    # locks/fix-<branch with / -> ->.lock, holder pid in <lock>/pid).  Probe the same lock
   371	    # the same way; a dead holder's lock does not block the merge.
   372	    lock = lock_dir() / ("fix-" + branch.replace("/", "-") + ".lock")
   373	    if lock.is_dir():
   374	        pid_text = ""
   375	        try:
   376	            pid_text = (lock / "pid").read_text(encoding="ascii").split()[0]
   377	        except (OSError, IndexError):
   378	            pass
   379	        if pid_text.isdigit() and _pid_alive(int(pid_text)):
   380	            raise GateFailure(f"gate 6 (fix loop): {lock} is held by live pid {pid_text}, required "
   381	                              "idle. autofix.sh is rewriting this branch and merging under it "
   382	                              "would race the fix commits.")
   383	    base_ref = None
   384	    for candidate in (f"github/{base}", f"refs/remotes/origin/{base}", base):
   385	        if git_ok(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{candidate}^{{commit}}"):
   386	            base_ref = candidate
   387	            break
   388	    if base_ref is None:
   389	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 7 (dependencies): no local ref resolves for base {base!r}, so "
   390	                          f"the merge-base commit range cannot be scanned. Run: git fetch "
   391	                          f"github {base}")
   392	    merge_base = git(repo_root, "merge-base", base_ref, head_sha)
   393	    # `git rev-list --format` prints a "commit <sha>" header before each formatted line.
   394	    lines = git(repo_root, "rev-list", "--format=%s", f"{merge_base}..{head_sha}").splitlines()
   395	    iterations = sum(1 for line in lines if not line.startswith("commit ")
   396	                     and line.startswith(FIX_COMMIT_PREFIXES))
   397	    passed(f"gate 6 fix loop idle; {iterations} fix-prefixed commit(s) since "
   398	           f"{merge_base[:12]} (autofix.sh bounds its own loop)")
   399	    return merge_base

   402	def check_dependencies(repo_root: Path, number: int, body: str,
   403	                       merge_base: str, head_sha: str,
   404	                       deferred_issues: set[int]) -> None:
   405	    """Gate 7 — nothing this PR closes may still have open children.
   406	
   407	    GitHub honors closing keywords in the PR body AND in commit messages that
   408	    land on the default branch, so both surfaces are scanned.  (Qualified
   409	    ``owner/repo#N`` references are out of scope: single-repo project.)
   410	    """
   411	    surfaces = [body or ""]
   412	    surfaces.append(git(repo_root, "log", "--format=%B", f"{merge_base}..{head_sha}",
   413	                        check=False))

   415	                                for n in CLOSES_RE.findall(text)))
   416	    if conflicts := deferred_issues.intersection(int(ident) for ident in closes):
   417	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 7 (dependencies): PR #{number} also closes deferred issue(s) "
   418	                          f"{sorted(conflicts)}, which must remain open.")
   419	    for ident in closes:
   420	        children = gh_common.open_sub_issues(int(ident))
   421	        if children:
   422	            raise GateFailure(f"gate 7 (dependencies): PR #{number} closes #{ident}, which still "
   423	                              f"has open sub-issue(s) {', '.join('#%d' % c for c in children)}, "
   424	                              "required none. Finish or re-parent them first.")
   425	    passed("gate 7 " + (", ".join(f"#{i} has no open sub-issue" for i in closes)
   426	                        or "no 'Closes #N' footer; nothing to depend on"))

   429	def run_gate(repo_root: Path, number: int, *, adjudicated: bool,
   430	             integration_base: str | None = None) -> dict:
   431	    """Raise ``GateFailure`` unless the PR may merge; return the merge facts."""
   432	    pr = gh_common.pr_view(number)
   433	    state = pr.get("state")
   434	    if state != "open" or pr.get("merged"):
   435	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 1 (open PR): PR #{number} is state={state!r} "
   436	                          f"merged={bool(pr.get('merged'))}, required open and unmerged.")
   437	    if pr.get("draft") is not False:
   438	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 1 (open PR): PR #{number} reports draft={pr.get('draft')!r}, "
   439	                          "required exactly false. (A missing field means the API response "
   440	                          "changed shape — fail closed, don't guess.)")
   441	    head = pr.get("head") or {}
   442	    head_sha = str(head.get("sha") or "")
   443	    branch = str(head.get("ref") or "")
   444	    base = str((pr.get("base") or {}).get("ref") or "")
   445	    if not head_sha or not branch or not base:
   446	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 1 (open PR): PR #{number} reports head sha={head_sha!r} "
   447	                          f"ref={branch!r} base={base!r}; all three are required.")
   448	    passed(f"gate 1 open, not a draft: {branch} @ {head_sha[:12]} -> {base}")
   449	    ensure_mergeable_worktree(repo_root, branch, base, head_sha)
   450	    # Gate 2b — the head must contain the current base tip unless the base has
   451	    # advanced only through allowlisted passive telemetry records.  CI and review
   452	    # remain bound to the exact head.  Fetch first so "current" means GitHub's
   453	    # tip, not a stale local remote-tracking ref.  Trains instead require the
   454	    # frozen integration base to remain unchanged, even for passive telemetry.
   455	    if not git_ok(repo_root, "fetch", "github", base):
   456	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2b (fresh base): 'git fetch github {base}' failed; cannot "
   457	                          "verify the branch is up to date with the base.")
   458	    if integration_base is not None:
   459	        if base != "main" or git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "github/main") != integration_base:
   460	            raise GateFailure("gate 2b (train): main changed from the frozen integration base")
   461	    elif not head_is_fresh(repo_root, f"github/{base}", head_sha):

   463	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2b (fresh base): {base} is at {base_tip} and the PR head "
   464	                          f"{head_sha[:12]} neither contains it nor predates only tolerated "
   465	                          "passive telemetry changes. Merge or rebase the base into the "
   466	                          "branch, re-run CI and review on the new head, then merge.")
   467	    passed("gate 2b frozen integration base unchanged; combined-commit CI required"
   468	           if integration_base is not None else
   469	           f"gate 2b head is fresh against current {base} "
   470	           "(ancestry or passive-telemetry-only move)")

   472	    reviews = gh_common.pr_reviews(number)
   473	    check_ci(statuses, head_sha)
   474	    deferred_issues = check_review(repo_root, number, head_sha, reviews, statuses, adjudicated=adjudicated)

   476	    blockers = [r for r in reviews if r.get("state") == "CHANGES_REQUESTED"
   477	                and r.get("commit_id") == head_sha]
   478	    if blockers:
   479	        who = ", ".join(sorted({sanitize(str((r.get("user") or {}).get("login") or "?"), 40)
   480	                                for r in blockers}))
   481	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 5 (changes requested): {len(blockers)} CHANGES_REQUESTED "
   482	                          f"review(s) by {who} on {head_sha[:12]}, required none. Adjudication "
   483	                          "never overrides this: dismiss it on GitHub, or fix and re-review.")
   484	    passed("gate 5 no CHANGES_REQUESTED review on this head")
   485	    merge_base = check_fix_gates(repo_root, branch, base, head_sha)
   486	    check_dependencies(repo_root, number, str(pr.get("body") or ""), merge_base, head_sha,
   487	                       deferred_issues)
   488	    return {"pr": pr, "head_sha": head_sha, "branch": branch, "base": base}

   493	def fast_forward_base(repo_root: Path, base: str) -> bool:
   494	    """Move local ``base`` onto the merge GitHub just made, if it is strictly behind: a
   495	    local commit GitHub has not seen is somebody's unpushed work, not this tail's call.
   496	    Returns True only when local ``base`` verifiably sits on the fetched remote."""
   497	    remote = f"github/{base}"
   498	    if not git_ok(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{remote}^{{commit}}"):
   499	        sys.stderr.write(f"warning: {remote} does not resolve after the fetch; local {base} "
   500	                         "left where it was\n")
   501	        return False
   502	    if not git_ok(repo_root, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", base, remote):
   503	        sys.stderr.write(f"warning: local {base} is not an ancestor of {remote}, so it is not "
   504	                         "moved — diverged history is a human's call, and the merge is already "
   505	                         "recorded on GitHub\n")
   506	        return False
   507	    if git_ok(repo_root, "merge", "--ff-only", remote):
   508	        sys.stdout.write(f"{base} fast-forwarded to "
   509	                         f"{git(repo_root, 'rev-parse', '--short', base, check=False)}\n")
   510	        return True
   511	    sys.stderr.write(f"warning: could not fast-forward {base}; by hand: git merge "
   512	                     f"--ff-only {remote}\n")
   513	    return False

   546	def remove_branch_and_worktree(repo_root: Path, branch: str) -> None:
   547	    """Drop the branch worktree, then the branch itself, under the old safeguards."""
   548	    lake_root = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT")
   549	    listing = git(repo_root, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain", check=False)
   550	    target: str | None = None
   551	    current_path: str | None = None
   552	    for line in listing.splitlines():
   553	        if line.startswith("worktree "):
   554	            current_path = line[len("worktree "):]
   555	        elif line.startswith("branch ") and line[len("branch "):] == f"refs/heads/{branch}":
   556	            target = current_path
   557	    if not target:
   558	        sys.stderr.write(f"warning: no worktree found for {branch}; attempting .lake cleanup\n")
   559	    elif git_ok(repo_root, "worktree", "remove", target):
   560	        sys.stdout.write(f"removed worktree {target}\n")
   561	    else:
   562	        sys.stderr.write(f"warning: could not remove worktree {target} (uncommitted files?); "
   563	                         f"by hand: git worktree remove --force {target}\n")

615	def run_merge(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
   616	    repo_root = args.repo_root.resolve()
   617	    number = int(args.pr)
   618	    # The exact-SHA REST guard is the real protection against a concurrent merge; this
   619	    # lock only keeps two local sessions from gating in lockstep.
   620	    with file_lock(f"pr-{number}"):
   621	        gate = run_gate(repo_root, number, adjudicated=args.adjudicated)
   622	        head_sha, branch, base = gate["head_sha"], gate["branch"], gate["base"]
   623	        title = sanitize(str(gate["pr"].get("title") or branch), TITLE_LIMIT)
   624	        passed(f"gate passed: PR #{number} {title} @ {head_sha[:12]} -> {base}")
   625	        if args.check_only:
   626	            return 0
   627	        if args.dry_run:
   628	            sys.stdout.write(f"[dry-run] would merge PR #{number} at {head_sha} (REST PUT with "
   629	                             "the exact-sha guard); GitHub would close the linked issues\n"
   630	                             f"[dry-run] would fetch github, fast-forward {base}, refresh "
   631	                             f"refs/remotes/origin/{base}, warm the cache, then remove the "
   632	                             f"worktree and branch {branch}\n")
   633	            return 0
   634	        sys.stdout.write(f"merged as {gh_common.merge_pr(number, head_sha)}; GitHub closed "
   635	                         "the linked issues\n")
   636	    try:
   637	        post_merge(repo_root, base, branch, warm_cache=not args.no_warm_cache)
   638	    except LayerError as exc:
   639	        sys.stderr.write(f"warning: post-merge housekeeping incomplete: {exc}\n")
   640	    return 0

    80	def sanitize(text: str | None, limit: int | None = None) -> str:

    82	
    83	    Verbatim port of the ``Sanitize issue content`` step at

    88	    fenced block that frames it as data.

    97	def check_bracket_free(value: str, what: str, chars: str = FORBIDDEN_TITLE_CHARS) -> None:

    99	
   100	    docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124: "Avoid prefixes like ``[Chapter 9] ...``:
   101	    bot-generated branch names inherit those characters, and ``]`` breaks part
   102	    of the PR automation stack."  Slugs and branch names derive from titles
   103	    mechanically, so the rule is enforced at the point of creation.
   104	    """
   105	    bad = sorted({c for c in value if c in chars})
   106	    if bad:
   107	        rendered = " ".join(repr(c) for c in bad)

   109	            f"{what} contains reserved character(s) {rendered}: {value!r}\n"

   111	            "automation (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). Rewrite the text, e.g. "

   117	    """Lowercase, hyphenated, bracket-free slug derived from a title."""
   118	    lowered = title.lower()
   119	    words = [w for w in re.split(r"[^a-z0-9]+", lowered) if w]
   120	    if not words:
   121	        raise LayerError(f"title {title!r} yields an empty slug; use words a-z0-9")

   123	    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*", slug):
   124	        raise LayerError(f"derived slug {slug!r} is not bracket-free lowercase-kebab")

   131	
   132	_HELD: dict[str, int] = {}
   133	
   134	
   135	@contextmanager
   136	def file_lock(name: str, *, timeout_note: str | None = None) -> Iterator[None]:
   137	    """Exclusive advisory lock under ``~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/<name>``.
   138	
   139	    The hazard is two agent sessions mutating the same runtime state; a
   140	    per-entity ``flock`` plus the atomic writer below covers it.  Re-entrant
   141	    within one process so a caller may hold a lock while a helper re-acquires
   142	    it.
   143	    """
   144	    if _HELD.get(name):
   145	        _HELD[name] += 1
   146	        try:
   147	            yield
   148	        finally:
   149	            _HELD[name] -= 1
   150	        return
   151	
   152	    directory = lock_dir()
   153	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   154	    path = directory / f"{name}.lock"
   155	    fd = os.open(str(path), os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o644)
   156	    try:
   157	        try:
   158	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
   159	        except OSError as exc:
   160	            if exc.errno not in (errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES):
   161	                raise
   162	            sys.stderr.write(f"waiting for lock {path} ...\n")
   163	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
   164	        os.ftruncate(fd, 0)
   165	        os.write(fd, f"{os.getpid()}\n".encode())
   166	        _HELD[name] = 1
   167	        try:
   168	            yield
   169	        finally:
   170	            _HELD.pop(name, None)
   171	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
   172	    finally:
   173	        os.close(fd)

   176	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   177	# Atomic writes
   178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   179	
   180	def atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
   181	    """Write *text* to *path* via tempfile + ``os.replace``.
   182	
   183	    Used for runtime artifacts and telemetry snapshots: a half-written file
   184	    must never be observable.
   185	    """
   186	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   187	    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(path.parent), prefix=f".{path.name}.", suffix=".tmp")
   188	    try:
   189	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   190	            handle.write(text)
   191	            handle.flush()
   192	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
   193	        os.replace(tmp, path)
   194	    except BaseException:
   195	        try:
   196	            os.unlink(tmp)
   197	        except OSError:
   198	            pass
   199	        raise
   200	    dir_fd = os.open(str(path.parent), os.O_RDONLY)
   201	    try:
   202	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
   203	    finally:
   204	        os.close(dir_fd)

    17	      "$base/hot-main/snapshots" "$base/hot-main/current"; do
    18	    protected="$(realpath -m -- "$protected")" || die "cannot resolve shared cache"
    19	    [ "$protected" != "/" ] || die "a protected shared-cache path resolves to /"
    20	    paths_overlap "$1" "$protected" && die "Lake target overlaps shared cache: $protected"

    23	canonical_lake_root() { # <create: 0|1>
    24	  local create="$1" root="${MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT:-}"

    26	  case "$root" in /*) ;; *) die "MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT must be absolute: $root" ;; esac
    27	  root="$(realpath -m -- "$root")" || die "cannot resolve MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT"

   112	  log "removed external Lake directory $target"
   113	}
   114	usage() { printf '%s\n' 'Usage: lake-root.sh prepare <tree> [--check] | cleanup <repo> <branch>'; }

    66	        capture_output=True,

    74	def run_git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> bytes:
    75	    """Run Git in ``repo`` and return stdout, or raise an operator-facing error."""
    76	
    77	    result = subprocess.run(
    78	        ["git", "-C", os.fspath(repo), *args],
    79	        check=False,
    80	        capture_output=True,
    81	        env=git_environment(),
    82	    )
    83	    if result.returncode != 0:
    84	        detail = os.fsdecode(result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip())
    85	        raise GuardError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed ({result.returncode}): {detail}")

    89	def resolve(repo: Path, revision: str) -> str:
    90	    """Resolve ``revision`` to one commit object name."""
    91	
    92	    return os.fsdecode(run_git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{revision}^{{commit}}").strip())

    95	def read_tree(repo: Path, revision: str) -> dict[bytes, TreeEntry]:
    96	    """Read every non-directory entry from ``revision`` without path decoding."""
    97	
    98	    entries: dict[bytes, TreeEntry] = {}
    99	    output = run_git(repo, "ls-tree", "-rz", "--full-tree", revision)
   100	    for record in output.split(b"\0"):
   101	        if not record:
   102	            continue
   103	        metadata, path = record.split(b"\t", 1)
   104	        mode, _kind, object_id = metadata.split(b" ", 2)
   105	        entries[path] = TreeEntry(mode, object_id)

   109	def read_index(repo: Path) -> dict[bytes, TreeEntry]:
   110	    """Read the stage-zero index used to create a pending merge commit."""
   111	
   112	    entries: dict[bytes, TreeEntry] = {}
   113	    output = run_git(repo, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
   114	    for record in output.split(b"\0"):
   115	        if not record:
   116	            continue
   117	        metadata, path = record.split(b"\t", 1)
   118	        mode, object_id, stage = metadata.split(b" ", 2)
   119	        if stage != b"0":
   120	            raise GuardError(
   121	                f"unresolved index entry at {os.fsdecode(path)!r} (stage {os.fsdecode(stage)})"
   122	            )
   123	        entries[path] = TreeEntry(mode, object_id)
   124	    return entries

   127	def read_index_state(repo: Path) -> tuple[dict[bytes, TreeEntry], frozenset[bytes]]:
   128	    """Read clean index entries and the paths retaining conflict stages."""
   129	
   130	    entries: dict[bytes, TreeEntry] = {}
   131	    conflicts: set[bytes] = set()
   132	    output = run_git(repo, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
   133	    for record in output.split(b"\0"):
   134	        if not record:
   135	            continue
   136	        metadata, path = record.split(b"\t", 1)
   137	        mode, object_id, stage = metadata.split(b" ", 2)
   138	        if stage == b"0":
   139	            entries[path] = TreeEntry(mode, object_id)
   140	        else:
   141	            conflicts.add(path)

   145	def merge_bases(repo: Path, branch: str, incoming: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:

   148	    bases = run_git(repo, "merge-base", "--all", branch, incoming).splitlines()

   154	def pending_merge_head(repo: Path) -> str | None:
   155	    """Return the sole pending ``MERGE_HEAD``, or ``None`` outside a merge."""
   156	
   157	    git_path = os.fsdecode(run_git(repo, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "MERGE_HEAD").strip())
   158	    path = Path(git_path)

   169	def pending_conflicts(repo: Path) -> frozenset[bytes]:

   175	        path = repo / path

   177	        return frozenset()

   181	        stripped = line.lstrip(b"#").strip()
   182	        if stripped == b"Conflicts:":
   183	            in_conflicts = True
   184	            continue
   185	        if in_conflicts:
   186	            if not line.startswith(b"#") or not stripped:

   192	def reconstructed_merge(
   193	    repo: Path, branch: str, incoming: str
   194	) -> tuple[dict[bytes, TreeEntry], frozenset[bytes]]:
   195	    """Recover Git's clean merge entries and conflicts in a disposable local clone."""

   197	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="mipstarre-merge-audit-") as directory:
   198	        clone = Path(directory) / "repo"
   199	        clone_result = subprocess.run(
   200	            [
   201	                "git",
   202	                "clone",
   203	                "--quiet",
   204	                "--shared",
   205	                "--no-checkout",
   206	                os.fspath(repo),
   207	                os.fspath(clone),
   208	            ],
   209	            check=False,
   210	            capture_output=True,
   211	            env=git_environment(),
   212	        )
   213	        if clone_result.returncode != 0:
   214	            detail = os.fsdecode(clone_result.stderr.strip() or clone_result.stdout.strip())
   215	            raise GuardError(f"temporary local clone failed: {detail}")
   216	        run_git(clone, "config", "user.email", "merge-loss-guard@example.invalid")
   217	        run_git(clone, "config", "user.name", "MIPStarRE merge-loss guard")
   218	        run_git(clone, "checkout", "--quiet", "--detach", branch)
   219	        merge_result = subprocess.run(
   220	            ["git", "-C", os.fspath(clone), "merge", "--no-commit", "--no-ff", incoming],
   221	            check=False,
   222	            capture_output=True,
   223	            env=git_environment(),
   224	        )
   225	        merge_head_output = run_git(clone, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "MERGE_HEAD").strip()
   226	        merge_head = Path(os.fsdecode(merge_head_output))
   227	        if not merge_head.is_absolute():
   228	            merge_head = clone / merge_head
   229	        if merge_result.returncode not in (0, 1) or not merge_head.is_file():
   230	            detail = os.fsdecode(merge_result.stderr.strip() or merge_result.stdout.strip())
   231	            raise GuardError(f"automatic merge reconstruction failed: {detail}")

   235	def pending_trees(repo: Path) -> tuple[MergeTrees, tuple[str, ...], str, str]:
   236	    """Load a pending merge's base, pre-merge branch, incoming, and index trees."""
   237	
   238	    incoming = pending_merge_head(repo)
   239	    if incoming is None:
   240	        raise GuardError("no merge is in progress")
   241	    branch = resolve(repo, "HEAD")
   242	    bases = merge_bases(repo, branch, incoming)
   243	    automatic = None
   244	    conflicts = pending_conflicts(repo)
   245	    if len(bases) > 1:
   246	        automatic, reconstructed = reconstructed_merge(repo, branch, incoming)
   247	        conflicts |= reconstructed
   248	    trees = MergeTrees(
   249	        bases=tuple(read_tree(repo, base) for base in bases),
   250	        branch=read_tree(repo, branch),
   251	        incoming=read_tree(repo, incoming),
   252	        result=read_index(repo),
   253	        conflicts=conflicts,
   254	        automatic=automatic,
   255	    )
   256	    return trees, bases, branch, incoming

   259	def committed_trees(
   260	    repo: Path, revision: str
   261	) -> tuple[MergeTrees, tuple[str, ...], str, str]:
   262	    """Load the four trees associated with a committed two-parent merge."""
   263	
   264	    commit = resolve(repo, revision)
   265	    topology = os.fsdecode(run_git(repo, "rev-list", "--parents", "-n", "1", commit)).split()
   266	    parents = topology[1:]
   267	    if len(parents) != 2:
   268	        raise GuardError(f"{commit} is not a two-parent merge commit")
   269	    branch, incoming = parents
   270	    bases = merge_bases(repo, branch, incoming)
   271	    automatic, conflicts = (
   272	        (None, frozenset())
   273	        if incoming in bases
   274	        else reconstructed_merge(repo, branch, incoming)
   275	    )
   276	    trees = MergeTrees(
   277	        bases=tuple(read_tree(repo, base) for base in bases),
   278	        branch=read_tree(repo, branch),
   279	        incoming=read_tree(repo, incoming),
   280	        result=read_tree(repo, commit),
   281	        conflicts=conflicts,
   282	        automatic=automatic if len(bases) > 1 else None,
   283	    )
   284	    return trees, bases, branch, incoming
   285	
   286	
   287	def inspect(trees: MergeTrees) -> list[Finding]:
   288	    """Find incoming paths deleted or wholly reverted by the result.
   289	
   290	    Deletion is branch-owned only when the path existed at a merge base and is
   291	    absent from the pre-merge branch tree. Recorded conflicts are exempt.
   292	    For multiple bases, Git's reconstructed clean result identifies incoming-only
   293	    changes without comparing against incompatible raw bases. Combined changes
   294	    remain the responsibility of normal review.
   295	    """
   296	
   297	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   298	    paths = set(trees.branch) | set(trees.incoming) | set(trees.result)
   299	    for base in trees.bases:
   300	        paths.update(base)
   301	    for path in sorted(paths):
   302	        if path in trees.conflicts:
   303	            continue
   304	        base_entries = tuple(base.get(path) for base in trees.bases)
   305	        branch_entry = trees.branch.get(path)
   306	        incoming_entry = trees.incoming.get(path)
   307	        result_entry = trees.result.get(path)
   308	
   309	        if incoming_entry is not None and result_entry is None:
   310	            branch_deleted = (
   311	                any(entry is not None for entry in base_entries) and branch_entry is None
   312	            )
   313	            if not branch_deleted:
   314	                findings.append(Finding("deleted", path))
   315	            continue
   316	
   317	        if trees.automatic is not None:
   318	            if (
   319	                incoming_entry != branch_entry
   320	                and trees.automatic.get(path) == incoming_entry
   321	                and result_entry == branch_entry
   322	            ):
   323	                findings.append(Finding("reverted", path))
   324	            continue
   325	
   326	        incoming_changed = all(incoming_entry != entry for entry in base_entries)
   327	        if not incoming_changed or result_entry == incoming_entry:
   328	            continue
   329	        branch_matches_base = all(branch_entry == entry for entry in base_entries)
   330	        if branch_matches_base and result_entry == branch_entry:
   331	            findings.append(Finding("reverted", path))
   332	    return findings
   333	
   334	
   335	def short(object_id: str) -> str:
   336	    return object_id[:12]
   337	
   338	
   339	def report(
   340	    findings: list[Finding], bases: tuple[str, ...], branch: str, incoming: str
   341	) -> int:
   342	    """Print a stable refusal report and return the intended process status."""
   343	
   344	    if not findings:
   345	        print(
   346	            "MIPStarRE merge-loss guard: ok "
   347	            f"(base {','.join(short(base) for base in bases)}, "
   348	            f"branch {short(branch)}, incoming {short(incoming)})."
   349	        )
   350	        return 0
   351	
   352	    print("MIPStarRE merge-loss guard: refusing a result that discards incoming changes.")
   353	    print(f"  merge base(s):   {', '.join(bases)}")
   354	    print(f"  pre-merge branch: {branch}")
   355	    print(f"  incoming head:   {incoming}")
   356	    for finding in findings:
   357	        print(f"  {finding.kind.upper():8} {os.fsdecode(finding.path)}")
   358	    print(
   359	        "Outside recorded conflicts, a missing path is permitted only when it existed "
   360	        "at the merge base and the pre-merge branch deleted it. Restore or combine the incoming content "
   361	        "before committing."
   362	    )
   363	    return 1
   364	
   365	
   366	def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
   367	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
   368	    parser.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, default=Path.cwd(), help="Git worktree root")
   369	    parser.add_argument(
   370	        "--commit",
   371	        metavar="REV",
   372	        help="audit an existing two-parent merge instead of the pending index",
   373	    )
   374	    return parser.parse_args(argv)
   375	
   376	
   377	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   378	    args = parse_args(argv)
   379	    repo = args.repo.resolve()
   380	    try:
   381	        if args.commit is None:
   382	            incoming = pending_merge_head(repo)
   383	            if incoming is None:
   384	                return 0
   385	            trees, bases, branch, incoming = pending_trees(repo)
   386	        else:
   387	            trees, bases, branch, incoming = committed_trees(repo, args.commit)
   388	        return report(inspect(trees), bases, branch, incoming)
   389	    except GuardError as error:
   390	        print(f"MIPStarRE merge-loss guard: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
   391	        return 2
   392	
   393	
   394	if __name__ == "__main__":
   395	    raise SystemExit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# usage: local/bin/ci.sh <pr-number> [options]
     4	#
     5	#   Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-ci.yml.  Runs the same eight
     6	#   jobs (build, blueprint-render, paper-gaps, blueprint-sync, file-length,
     7	#   proof-debt, proof-evasion, statement-origin) against the worktree of the
     8	#   PR's branch, with the same per-area change gating, and records the result
     9	#   where GitHub is the source of truth: one `local-ci/<step>` commit status
    10	#   per step plus `local-ci/summary`, all bound to the exact tested head SHA,
    11	#   and one idempotent manifest comment on the PR.
    12	#
    13	#   <pr-number>        GitHub PR number (7 or 0007).  There is no prs/ tree
    14	#                      any more; the branch and base come from the PR itself
    15	#                      via local/bin/gh_common.py pr-view.
    16	#
    17	#   --worktree PATH    Use PATH as the branch worktree instead of resolving it
    18	#                      from `git worktree list` / .worktrees/<branch>.
    19	#   --base REF         Override the base branch reported by GitHub (default:
    20	#                      the PR's base ref, else main).
    21	#   --integration-head SHA  Check a local train commit, without a PR argument.
    22	#                      Requires --worktree and --base SHA; runs every step and
    23	#                      publishes no PR statuses or reviews. No skip flags allowed.
    24	#   --only STEP        Run only STEP (repeatable).  Gating still applies unless
    25	#                      --force-all is given.  Makes the run PARTIAL.
    26	#   --force-all        Ignore change gating; run every step.
    27	#   --skip-build       Record the build step as skipped (operator override for
    28	#                      a machine that must not compile right now).  Makes the
    29	#                      run PARTIAL.
    30	#   --dry-run          Resolve, gate and print the plan; run nothing, write
    31	#                      nothing, post nothing.
    32	#   -h, --help         This message.
    33	#
    34	# Outputs
    35	#   local-ci/<step> + local-ci/summary     commit statuses on the tested SHA
    36	#   PR comment <!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->   step table + manifest JSON
    37	#   ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-manifests/pr<N>-<sha>.json    per-step manifest
    38	#   ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<N>/<sha>/<step>.log     step logs (runtime)
    39	#   results/telemetry/builds.jsonl         one ci-build line when build ran
    40	#
    41	#   A PARTIAL run (--only / --skip-build / --dry-run) posts NOTHING to GitHub
    42	#   and writes <sha>.partial.json instead: a debugging run must not be able to
    43	#   hand the review or merge gate a verdict it did not earn.
    44	#
    45	# Exit status

   117	# Locks are advisory mkdir-based lease directories, matching the hot-main
   118	# writer lease convention in local/protocols/build-cache.md.
   119	HELD_LOCKS=""
   120	
   121	lock_age_s() {
   122	  # $1 = lock dir.  Prints the age in seconds of its owner stamp, or a huge
   123	  # number when the stamp is unreadable (treat as stale).
   124	  local _stamp="$1/owner"
   125	  if [ ! -f "$_stamp" ]; then
   126	    printf '%s\n' 999999999
   127	    return 0
   128	  fi
   129	  local _mtime
   130	  _mtime="$(stat -f %m "$_stamp" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$_stamp" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
   131	  printf '%s\n' "$(( $(epoch_now) - _mtime ))"
   132	}
   133	
   134	lock_owner_alive() {
   135	  local _stamp="$1/owner"
   136	  [ -f "$_stamp" ] || return 1
   137	  local _pid
   138	  _pid="$(head -n 1 "$_stamp" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   139	  case "$_pid" in
   140	    ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;;
   141	  esac
   142	  kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
   143	}
   144	
   145	# acquire_lock <dir> <wait_seconds> <stale_seconds> <tag>
   146	# Returns 0 on success, 1 on timeout.  A lock whose owner process is ALIVE is
   147	# NEVER broken, regardless of age: the parent workflow exempts main-branch
   148	# (cache-seeding) runs from cancellation, and the local analog is that a
   149	# running full build is always allowed to finish (the initial cold build took
   150	# ~7 h; see results/telemetry/builds.jsonl).  The stale threshold applies only
   151	# when the owner stamp is unreadable, so an interrupted mkdir cannot wedge the
   152	# machine forever.
   153	acquire_lock() {
   154	  local _dir="$1" _wait="$2" _stale="$3" _tag="$4"
   155	  local _waited=0
   156	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$_dir")"
   157	  while ! mkdir "$_dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   158	    if lock_owner_alive "$_dir"; then
   159	      : # live owner: wait below, never break
   160	    elif [ -f "$_dir/owner" ] || [ -f "$_dir/info" ]; then
   161	      warn "breaking stale lock $_dir (owner process is dead)"
   162	      rm -rf "$_dir"
   163	      continue
   164	    elif [ "$(lock_age_s "$_dir")" -gt "$_stale" ]; then
   165	      warn "breaking stale lock $_dir (no owner stamp, older than ${_stale}s)"
   166	      rm -rf "$_dir"
   167	      continue
   168	    fi
   169	    if [ "$_waited" -ge "$_wait" ]; then
   170	      return 1
   171	    fi
   172	    if [ "$_waited" -eq 0 ]; then
   173	      info "waiting for lock $_dir (held by pid $(head -n 1 "$_dir/owner" 2>/dev/null || echo '?'))"
   174	    fi
   175	    sleep 5
   176	    _waited=$(( _waited + 5 ))
   177	  done
   178	  printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$$" "$(iso_now)" "$_tag" > "$_dir/owner"
   179	  HELD_LOCKS="$HELD_LOCKS $_dir"
   180	  return 0
   181	}
   182	
   183	release_lock() {
   184	  local _dir="$1" _kept="" _held
   185	  for _held in $HELD_LOCKS; do
   186	    if [ "$_held" = "$_dir" ]; then
   187	      rm -rf "$_held"
   188	    else
   189	      _kept="$_kept $_held"
   190	    fi
   191	  done
   192	  HELD_LOCKS="$_kept"
   193	}
   194	
   195	RUN_TMP=""
   196	cleanup() {
   197	  local _lock
   198	  for _lock in $HELD_LOCKS; do
   199	    rm -rf "$_lock" 2>/dev/null || true
   200	  done
   201	  if [ -n "$RUN_TMP" ] && [ -d "$RUN_TMP" ]; then
   202	    rm -rf "$RUN_TMP"
   203	  fi
   204	}

   214	"""Manifest and telemetry helper for local/bin/ci.sh.
   215	
   216	Two subcommands, both writing atomically (tempfile in the destination
   217	directory + os.replace) so a crashed or killed CI run never leaves a
   218	half-written manifest or a torn telemetry line behind:
   219	
   220	  manifest        assemble the per-SHA CI manifest from a step TSV
   221	  telemetry       append one JSON line to results/telemetry/*.jsonl
   222	
   223	There is no frontmatter subcommand any more: the PR record lives on GitHub,
   224	and the run's verdict is published as commit statuses plus the manifest

   239	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   240	# Atomic write
   241	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   242	
   243	
   244	def atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
   245	    """Write *text* to *path* via a same-directory tempfile and os.replace."""
   246	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   247	    handle, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
   248	        dir=str(path.parent), prefix=path.name + ".", suffix=".tmp"
   249	    )
   250	    try:
   251	        with os.fdopen(handle, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
   252	            stream.write(text)
   253	            stream.flush()
   254	            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
   255	        os.replace(tmp_name, path)
   256	    except BaseException:
   257	        try:
   258	            os.unlink(tmp_name)
   259	        except OSError:
   260	            pass
   261	        raise

   265	# Manifest
   266	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   269	def read_steps(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
   270	    """Parse the tab-separated step records ci.sh appends as it runs."""
   271	    steps: list[dict] = []
   272	    if not path.exists():
   273	        return steps
   274	    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
   275	        if not line.strip():
   276	            continue
   277	        fields = line.split("\t")
   278	        while len(fields) < 6:
   279	            fields.append("")
   280	        step, outcome, seconds, log_path, blocking, note = fields[:6]
   281	        steps.append(
   282	            {
   283	                "step": step,
   284	                "outcome": outcome,
   285	                "seconds": int(seconds or 0),
   286	                "log_path": log_path,
   287	                "blocking": blocking == "1",
   288	                "note": note,
   289	            }
   290	        )
   291	    return steps
   292	
   293	
   294	def read_lines(path: Path | None) -> list[str]:
   295	    if path is None or not path.exists():
   296	        return []
   297	    return [line for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]

   342	def cmd_telemetry(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""The one GitHub layer for ``local/bin`` — a thin, fail-closed wrapper over ``gh``.
     3	
     4	GitHub is the single source of truth for issues and their prerequisite edges,
     5	PRs, CI evidence (commit statuses on the exact head SHA), review verdicts
     6	(COMMENT reviews bound to a commit id), and merges (REST merge guarded by an
     7	exact-SHA match).  This module is the only place workflow scripts talk to
     8	GitHub, as a Python import or via its CLI
     9	(``gh_common.py <subcommand> ...``) from shell.
    10	
    11	Design rules (local/protocols/issues-prs.md):
    12	
    13	* At most one write mutation per invocation of a helper; ambiguity after a
    14	  failed write is resolved by re-reading state and adopting, never by
    15	  repeating the mutation.  Writes that are idempotent by content (statuses,
    16	  close-PATCH) may be retried blindly.
    17	* Everything uses ``gh api`` (raw REST), so no feature of a modern ``gh`` CLI
    18	  is required — the exact-SHA merge guard is the REST ``sha`` parameter, not a
    19	  CLI flag.
    20	* Fail closed: a network failure after retries raises; no local fallback
    21	  record is ever written.
    22	
    23	Environment: ``MIPSTARRE_GH`` (gh binary; default ``gh`` on PATH, then
    24	``~/.local/bin/gh``), ``MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO`` (``owner/repo``; default
    25	parsed from the ``github`` remote of the primary checkout).

    91	def run_gh(args: list[str], *, input_text: str | None = None,
    92	           mutation: bool = False, idempotent: bool = False,
    93	           retries: int = 3) -> str:
    94	    """Run ``gh`` and return stdout; raise ``LayerError`` on final failure.
    95	
    96	    A non-idempotent mutation is attempted exactly once — the caller owns
    97	    ambiguity recovery by re-reading state.  Reads and idempotent mutations
    98	    retry on transient failures with linear backoff.
    99	    """
   100	    attempts = 1 if (mutation and not idempotent) else max(1, retries)
   101	    env = dict(os.environ, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED="1", GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER="1",
   102	               NO_COLOR="1", GH_PAGER="cat")
   103	    last_err = ""
   104	    for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
   105	        proc = subprocess.run(
   106	            [gh_bin(), *args], input=input_text,
   107	            capture_output=True, text=True, env=env,
   108	        )
   109	        if proc.returncode == 0:
   110	            return proc.stdout
   111	        last_err = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout or "").strip()
   112	        if attempt < attempts and _TRANSIENT_RE.search(last_err):
   113	            time.sleep(5 * attempt)
   114	            continue
   115	        break
   116	    raise LayerError(f"gh {' '.join(args[:3])}... failed: {last_err[:2000]}")

   119	def api(path: str, *, method: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None,
   120	        paginate: bool = False, mutation: bool = False,
   121	        idempotent: bool = False, absolute: bool = False):
   122	    """Call the REST API under ``repos/<slug>/`` (or an absolute *path*).
   123	
   124	    Pagination is manual (``?per_page=100&page=N``) so nothing here depends on
   125	    a modern ``gh``.  Returns parsed JSON (``None`` for an empty response).
   126	    """
   127	    full = path if absolute else f"repos/{repo_slug()}/{path}"
   128	
   129	    def one(page_path: str):
   130	        args = ["api", page_path]
   131	        if method:
   132	            args += ["-X", method]
   133	        input_text = None
   134	        if payload is not None:
   135	            args += ["--input", "-"]
   136	            input_text = json.dumps(payload)
   137	        out = run_gh(args, input_text=input_text, mutation=mutation,
   138	                     idempotent=idempotent)
   139	        return json.loads(out) if out.strip() else None
   140	
   141	    if not paginate:
   142	        return one(full)
   143	
   144	    sep = "&" if "?" in full else "?"
   145	    rows: list = []
   146	    page = 1
   147	    while True:
   148	        batch = one(f"{full}{sep}per_page={PAGE}&page={page}")
   149	        if not batch:
   150	            break
   151	        rows.extend(batch)
   152	        if len(batch) < PAGE:
   153	            break
   154	        page += 1
   155	    return rows

   200	    add("--title", help="conventional-commit title; required to open a new PR")

   205	    add("--issue", type=int, metavar="N", help="append a 'Closes #N' body footer")

     2	#
     3	# github-sync.sh — push the named refs to this repository's GitHub home,
     4	# git@github.com:Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A.git (standalone repo since the
     5	# 2026-08-31 restructure; the old subtree-into-monorepo flow is retired, see
     6	# EVOLUTION.md), then refresh the read-only record snapshot.
     7	#
     8	# Usage: local/bin/github-sync.sh [ref ...]      (default: main)
     9	#
    10	# Run after every merge to main.  Only the named refs are pushed: `git push
    11	# --all` is deliberately gone.  GitHub now holds the records — issues, PRs, the
    12	# per-SHA CI statuses and the review verdicts (local/protocols/issues-prs.md) —
    13	# and a blanket push republishes every stale local branch, including the
    14	# throwaway fix branches whose heads those records are bound to.  Push what you
    15	# mean to publish.
    16	#
    17	# Exit codes:
    18	#   0  requested refs and any final main telemetry published; snapshot reads are best-effort
    19	#   1  a named ref or final telemetry publication failed, or snapshot commit failed
    20	set -euo pipefail
    21	
    22	PROG="github-sync.sh"
    23	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
    24	_common="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)"
    25	case "$_common" in */.git) ROOT="$(dirname "$_common")" ;; esac
    26	cd "$ROOT"
    27	LOCAL_BIN="$ROOT/local/bin"
    28	
    29	REFS=("$@")
    30	[ "${#REFS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || REFS=(main)
    31	
    32	git remote get-url github >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
    33	  git remote add github git@github.com:Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A.git
    34	
    35	RC=0
    36	MAIN_PUSHED=0
    37	for ref in "${REFS[@]}"; do
    38	  git rev-parse --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$ref" >/dev/null || {
    39	    echo "$PROG: no local branch '$ref'; skipping" >&2; RC=1; continue
    40	  }
    41	  pushed=0
    42	  for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    43	    if "$LOCAL_BIN/checked-push.sh" --repo-root "$ROOT" github \
    44	        "refs/heads/$ref:refs/heads/$ref"; then
    45	      echo "$PROG: pushed $ref ($(git rev-parse --short "$ref"))"
    46	      pushed=1
    47	      [ "$ref" != main ] || MAIN_PUSHED=1
    48	      break
    49	    fi
    50	    echo "$PROG: push attempt $i for '$ref' failed; retrying" >&2
    51	    sleep 15
    52	  done
    53	  [ "$pushed" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$PROG: all push attempts failed for '$ref'" >&2; RC=1; }
    54	done
    55	
    56	# Audit/recovery telemetry only — never lifecycle input (gh_common.py:390-392),
    57	# so a snapshot failure must not fail a successful push.
    58	if ! python3 "$LOCAL_BIN/gh_common.py" snapshot \
    59	      --out-dir "$ROOT/results/telemetry/github-snapshot"; then
    60	  echo "$PROG: warning: the GitHub record snapshot failed; the push above still stands" >&2
    61	fi
    62	# checked-push.sh requires the primary checkout to match the pushed commit
    63	# exactly, so the snapshot just written (and any build ledger rows) must be
    64	# committed before the next publish; otherwise every later push is refused.
    65	SNAPSHOT_COMMITTED=0
    66	if ! git -C "$ROOT" diff --quiet -- results/telemetry/github-snapshot results/telemetry/builds.jsonl 2>/dev/null; then
    67	  if git -C "$ROOT" commit -q -m "chore(telemetry): GitHub record snapshot" \
    68	    -- results/telemetry/github-snapshot results/telemetry/builds.jsonl; then
    69	    SNAPSHOT_COMMITTED=1
    70	  else
    71	    echo "$PROG: could not commit the snapshot; the next push will need a clean tree" >&2
    72	    RC=1
    73	  fi
    74	fi
    75	
    76	# Keep the snapshot after publication, but do not leave an explicitly requested
    77	# main ahead because of our own telemetry commit. Branch-only syncs keep their
    78	# original scope. This final push never generates another snapshot.
    79	if [ "$MAIN_PUSHED" -eq 1 ] && [ "$SNAPSHOT_COMMITTED" -eq 1 ]; then
    80	  if "$LOCAL_BIN/checked-push.sh" --repo-root "$ROOT" github \
    81	      refs/heads/main:refs/heads/main; then
    82	    echo "$PROG: published snapshot on main ($(git rev-parse --short main))"
    83	  else
    84	    echo "$PROG: snapshot commit remains local; final main publication failed" >&2
    85	    RC=1
    86	  fi
    87	fi
    88	
    89	exit "$RC"

   166	def run_train(repo: Path, numbers: list[int], adjudicated: set[int]) -> int:

   187	        print(f"train worktree: {worktree}", flush=True)

   147	def publication_outcome(repo: Path, head: str) -> str:
   148	    """Reconcile an ambiguous push without retrying it or assuming a failed read is absence."""
   149	    try:
   150	        rows = git(repo, "ls-remote", "github", "refs/heads/main").split()
   151	        if len(rows) != 2 or rows[1] != "refs/heads/main":
   152	            return "unknown"
   153	        remote = rows[0]
   154	        if remote == head:
   155	            return "published"
   156	        git(repo, "fetch", "--no-tags", "github", remote)
   157	        result = subprocess.run(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", head, remote], cwd=repo)
   158	        if result.returncode == 0:
   159	            return "published"
   160	        if result.returncode == 1 and git(repo, "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository") == "false":
   161	            return "refused"
   162	    except (LayerError, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   163	        print(f"publication reconciliation failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
   164	    return "unknown"

## 5. Review Checklist

Every PR touching Lean code should be reviewed against these criteria:

1. **Proof correctness** -- No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.
   Run `rg -n "sorry|axiom" <file>` to verify.

2. **Mathlib style** -- Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and
   `MATHLIB_doc` references. See the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review`
   reference for the full Mathlib review guide.

3. **Paper terminology** -- Public Lean names, module docstrings, declaration
   docstrings, and documentation-visible comments should use terminology from
   the paper and blueprint, not implementation history. See
   [mathematical_language.md](mathematical_language.md) for the project-local
   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag
   names that encode historical formalization status rather than mathematical
   content. When an old public identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR,
   record the required migration in the issue, PR description, or an audit file
   under [audits/](../audits/).
   New and substantively updated audit files should follow the term norm and
   format in
   [audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md](../audits/2026-04-29_audit-document-format.md).
   Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   public name.
   Review-fix PRs must read the relevant audit files under [audits/](../audits/)
   before changing names or prose. If an audit marks a naming migration or
   historical-formalization term as in scope for the fix, addressing it or
   explicitly updating the audit trail is a merge blocker.

4. **Linter hygiene** -- Linter-warning cleanup must fix warnings, not mask
   them with broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks. See
   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md#linter-warnings) for the project rule and the narrow
   exception policy.

5. **Type safety** -- No universe mismatches, coercion problems, or unresolved
   metavariables.

6. **Performance** -- Avoid expensive tactics on large types (e.g., `decide` on
   `Fin 1000`). Watch for timeout-prone proof terms.

7. **Modularity** -- Are new lemmas general enough to be reused? Could any be
   upstreamed to Mathlib?

8. **Documentation** -- Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.
   Module files should have a header comment with `## References` citing the
   relevant arXiv paper(s).

9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** -- If the PR formalizes a statement
   from the blueprint, add `\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\leanok` tags to the
   corresponding `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file. If the PR adds a public
   auxiliary lemma that is not a named statement in the original paper, record
   that explicitly: the Lean docstring should call it a formalization-only
   auxiliary lemma and the blueprint should either omit it as private/internal
   infrastructure or include it as a clearly subordinate support node connected
   by `\uses{...}`. See
   [blueprint_style_guide.md](blueprint_style_guide.md#recording-formalization-only-lemmas).
   PR descriptions and follow-up issues should cite the corresponding paper or
   blueprint path, line, label, and a short quotation or precise paraphrase.
   Reviewers should also check for early drift from the source: new hypotheses,
   weakened conclusions, changed quantifier order, altered error parameters,
   or renamed obligation structures that turn a paper theorem into a conditional
   theorem.  If such drift appears, request a statement integrity audit before
   reviewing the proof.  A bridge or residual hypothesis should be treated as
   proof debt to remove, not as evidence that the paper statement has been
   formalized.

10. **Scaffolding integrity** -- If the PR introduces or modifies scaffolded
   definitions (types, theorem statements with `sorry` proofs), verify that
   the types and API surface align with Mathlib. Scaffolding that uses custom
   types incompatible with Mathlib blocks future proof work. See
   the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and
   [project_conventions.md](project_conventions.md) for details.

11. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** -- Review against
   [anti_patterns.md](anti_patterns.md), which catalogues subtler failure
   modes that pass the proof-integrity blocker checks but still fail
   to prove the claimed mathematics: conclusion-shaped hypotheses (A1),
   `:= rfl` definitional sleight-of-hand (A2), zero-fallback branches
   hiding preconditions (A3), trivial default witnesses (A4),
   Mathlib-bypass castles (A5), and external `*Statement` smuggles (A6).
   Use the reviewer checklist at the end of that file.

12. **Proof frontier integrity** -- If the PR introduces or threads structure
   fields such as `*Input`, `*Residual`, `*BridgeInputs`, `*Witness`,
   `*Statement`, `*Conclusion`, or `*Package`, review it against
   [proof_frontier_review.md](proof_frontier_review.md). A PR that only
   repackages an assumption should not be described as proving the corresponding
   paper step; it must name the missing obligation discharger or link the native
   sub-issue that tracks it.  For source-labelled theorems, the preferred repair
   is to extract any usable proof content into source-faithful lemmas and
   restore the paper-aligned statement, even if the remaining proof is a tracked
   `sorry` during the cleanup.  For source-labelled proof gaps, also use the
   protocol in
   [paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex).

### Semantic scaffold checklist (required for core math objects)

For semantic objects such as measurements, submeasurements, distributions,
averaged operators, and packaged theorem outputs, reviewers should additionally
verify:

1. **Impossible states check** -- Does the structure exclude states that are
   impossible under the paper definition?
2. **Derived-field check** -- If a field is mathematically derived
   (e.g. `total = ∑ a, outcome a`), is it either derived on demand or stored
   together with an equality proof (e.g. `sum_eq_total`)?
3. **Invariant bundling check** -- Are core invariants (positivity,
   boundedness/normalization, completeness where applicable) encoded directly

   403	                       merge_base: str, head_sha: str,

   405	    """Gate 7 — nothing this PR closes may still have open children.
   406

   408	    land on the default branch, so both surfaces are scanned.  (Qualified
   409	    ``owner/repo#N`` references are out of scope: single-repo project.)
   410	    """

   412	    surfaces.append(git(repo_root, "log", "--format=%B", f"{merge_base}..{head_sha}",
   413	                        check=False))

   415	                                for n in CLOSES_RE.findall(text)))
   416	    if conflicts := deferred_issues.intersection(int(ident) for ident in closes):
   417	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 7 (dependencies): PR #{number} also closes deferred issue(s) "
   418	                          f"{sorted(conflicts)}, which must remain open.")
   419	    for ident in closes:
   420	        children = gh_common.open_sub_issues(int(ident))
   421	        if children:
   422	            raise GateFailure(f"gate 7 (dependencies): PR #{number} closes #{ident}, which still "
   423	                              f"has open sub-issue(s) {', '.join('#%d' % c for c in children)}, "
   424	                              "required none. Finish or re-parent them first.")
   425	    passed("gate 7 " + (", ".join(f"#{i} has no open sub-issue" for i in closes)

   493	def fast_forward_base(repo_root: Path, base: str) -> bool:
   494	    """Move local ``base`` onto the merge GitHub just made, if it is strictly behind: a
   495	    local commit GitHub has not seen is somebody's unpushed work, not this tail's call.
   496	    Returns True only when local ``base`` verifiably sits on the fetched remote."""
   497	    remote = f"github/{base}"
   498	    if not git_ok(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{remote}^{{commit}}"):
   499	        sys.stderr.write(f"warning: {remote} does not resolve after the fetch; local {base} "
   500	                         "left where it was\n")
   501	        return False
   502	    if not git_ok(repo_root, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", base, remote):
   503	        sys.stderr.write(f"warning: local {base} is not an ancestor of {remote}, so it is not "
   504	                         "moved — diverged history is a human's call, and the merge is already "
   505	                         "recorded on GitHub\n")
   506	        return False
   507	    if git_ok(repo_root, "merge", "--ff-only", remote):
   508	        sys.stdout.write(f"{base} fast-forwarded to "
   509	                         f"{git(repo_root, 'rev-parse', '--short', base, check=False)}\n")
   510	        return True
   511	    sys.stderr.write(f"warning: could not fast-forward {base}; by hand: git merge "
   512	                     f"--ff-only {remote}\n")
   513	    return False

  1217	# Publish to GitHub (FULL runs only)

  1219	# Order matters: per-step statuses first, then the freshness re-check, then

  1226	publish_step_statuses() {
  1227	  local _s _outcome _secs _log _blocking _note _state _desc

  1231	      success) _state=success; _desc="passed in ${_secs}s" ;;
  1232	      skipped) _state=success; _desc="skipped: ${_note:-not selected}" ;;
  1233	      failure) _state=failure; _desc="${_note:-failed} (${_secs}s)" ;;
  1234	      error)   _state=error;   _desc="${_note:-could not run}" ;;

   119	    words = [w for w in re.split(r"[^a-z0-9]+", lowered) if w]
   120	    if not words:
   121	        raise LayerError(f"title {title!r} yields an empty slug; use words a-z0-9")
   122	    slug = "-".join(words[:max_words])[:60].strip("-")
   123	    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*", slug):
   124	        raise LayerError(f"derived slug {slug!r} is not bracket-free lowercase-kebab")
   125	    return slug

   128	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   129	# Advisory locking
   130	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   131	
   132	_HELD: dict[str, int] = {}
   133	
   134	
   135	@contextmanager
   136	def file_lock(name: str, *, timeout_note: str | None = None) -> Iterator[None]:
   137	    """Exclusive advisory lock under ``~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/<name>``.
   138	
   139	    The hazard is two agent sessions mutating the same runtime state; a
   140	    per-entity ``flock`` plus the atomic writer below covers it.  Re-entrant
   141	    within one process so a caller may hold a lock while a helper re-acquires
   142	    it.
   143	    """
   144	    if _HELD.get(name):
   145	        _HELD[name] += 1
   146	        try:
   147	            yield
   148	        finally:
   149	            _HELD[name] -= 1
   150	        return
   151	
   152	    directory = lock_dir()
   153	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   154	    path = directory / f"{name}.lock"
   155	    fd = os.open(str(path), os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o644)
   156	    try:
   157	        try:
   158	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
   159	        except OSError as exc:
   160	            if exc.errno not in (errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES):
   161	                raise
   162	            sys.stderr.write(f"waiting for lock {path} ...\n")
   163	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
   164	        os.ftruncate(fd, 0)
   165	        os.write(fd, f"{os.getpid()}\n".encode())
   166	        _HELD[name] = 1
   167	        try:
   168	            yield
   169	        finally:
   170	            _HELD.pop(name, None)
   171	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
   172	    finally:
   173	        os.close(fd)
   174

   176	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   177	# Atomic writes
   178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   179	
   180	def atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
   181	    """Write *text* to *path* via tempfile + ``os.replace``.
   182	
   183	    Used for runtime artifacts and telemetry snapshots: a half-written file
   184	    must never be observable.
   185	    """
   186	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   187	    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(path.parent), prefix=f".{path.name}.", suffix=".tmp")
   188	    try:
   189	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   190	            handle.write(text)
   191	            handle.flush()
   192	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
   193	        os.replace(tmp, path)
   194	    except BaseException:
   195	        try:
   196	            os.unlink(tmp)
   197	        except OSError:
   198	            pass
   199	        raise
   200	    dir_fd = os.open(str(path.parent), os.O_RDONLY)
   201	    try:
   202	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
   203	    finally:
   204	        os.close(dir_fd)

   156	# The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround (docgen.yml:56-69): `lake exe cache get`
   157	# runs `lake update`, whose mathlib post-update hook prunes
   158	# .lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib before fetching a cloud release.  On
   159	# a tree that has never built, the directory does not exist and the uncaught
   160	# exception aborts the whole cache fetch.  The local variant of the same
   161	# fresh-state failure is a *dirty* vendored tree: build byproducts such as
   162	# widget/js/lake.trace block the revision checkout — see the 2026-08-30 failed
   163	# entry and its retry in results/telemetry/builds.jsonl.
   164	proofwidgets_fresh_state_workaround() { # <worktree>
   165	  local tree="$1" pkg name dirty=0
   166	  if [ ! -d "$tree/.lake/packages" ]; then
   167	    log "no .lake/packages yet (fresh worktree); warm-worktree.sh will fetch tier 2"
   168	    return 0
   169	  fi
   170	  # Only tracked modifications are reset.  `git clean` is deliberately NOT run
   171	  # inside a vendored package: it would delete downloaded build output and cost
   172	  # hours to refetch.  If an untracked byproduct still blocks the checkout, the
   173	  # cache fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from source.
   174	  for pkg in "$tree"/.lake/packages/*; do
   175	    [ -d "$pkg/.git" ] || continue
   176	    name="$(basename "$pkg")"
   177	    if [ -n "$(run_outside_git_env git -C "$pkg" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no 2>/dev/null || true)" ]; then
   178	      dirty=1
   179	      if [ "$CHECK_ONLY" -eq 1 ]; then
   180	        warn "vendored package tree $name is dirty; the Mathlib cache fetch will abort"
   181	        continue
   182	      fi
   183	      log "resetting dirty vendored package tree: $name"
   184	      run_outside_git_env git -C "$pkg" reset --hard >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   185	        || warn "could not reset $name; the Mathlib cache fetch may abort"
   186	    fi
   187	  done
   188	  if [ "$CHECK_ONLY" -eq 0 ]; then
   189	    if [ -d "$tree/.lake/packages/proofwidgets" ]; then
   190	      mkdir -p "$tree/.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib"
   191	    fi
   192	    # A dirty tree that was reset is fixed, not a finding.
   193	    return 0
   194	  fi
   195	  return "$dirty"
   196	}

   198	call_warm_worktree() { # <worktree> [args...]
   199	  local tree="$1"; shift
   200	  # Deliberately the copy next to THIS script, not the one inside the worktree:
   201	  # a worktree may hold an unreviewed branch, and the bootstrap must not execute
   202	  # code from the tree it is bootstrapping (the local analog of DESIGN.md #5).
   203	  local warmer="$SCRIPT_DIR/warm-worktree.sh"
   204	  if [ ! -f "$warmer" ]; then
   205	    die "warm-worktree.sh not found at $warmer.
   206	The build cache consumer is part of this bootstrap and has no fallback:
   207	without it this worktree would silently start from a cold build.
   208	Restore local/bin/warm-worktree.sh, or re-run with --skip-warm to accept that."
   209	  fi
   210	  if [ ! -x "$warmer" ]; then
   211	    warn "$warmer is not executable; invoking it through bash"
   212	    bash "$warmer" "$tree" "$@"
   213	    return $?
   214	  fi
   215	  "$warmer" "$tree" "$@"
   216	}

## Findings
- [ ] F1 (blocker) `local/bin/checked-push.sh:157` — The push leases only `main`, allowing a member ref to move after verification while stale member content is still published.
- [ ] F2 (changes) `local/bin/pr_train.py:171` — The private telemetry lock does not synchronize with canonical telemetry writers, so the train event can be lost.

## Review
F1 is reproducible. I injected a member-ref update after `verify_manifest` completed but immediately before `git push`. The train returned success, `main` received the previously verified member commit, and the member branch pointed elsewhere. The local `pr-N` locks cannot protect against remote pushes, and the transport transaction constrains only `refs/heads/main`. Publication needs an atomic server-side guard covering every member ref, or an equivalent mechanism, plus a test for movement at transport start.

For F2, `record()` uses `train-telemetry.lock` and directly appends to `events.md`. The canonical event writer uses `events-md.lock` with a read-modify-replace operation. Concurrent execution can therefore replace the file after the train append or cause the train writer to append to an unlinked inode. Use the canonical telemetry writer or its exact locking protocol.

The authoritative 1,287-line patch was read in full; the prior ledger contained no findings. Eleven focused train fixtures passed, including frozen-base, refusal, conflict, and ambiguous-push cases. Shell syntax, Python AST parsing, `git diff --check`, and final worktree cleanliness passed.

The review-round cap is reached. Under `local/protocols/review.md` §12, both findings must be fixed or assigned explicit tracked-issue dispositions before operator adjudication. F1 should be resolved before this publication path is deployed.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
